posts.title: Why we built this AI tool…
posts.message:
Hey Sumo-lings!

Me and my co-founder Naz have ADHD and are neurodivergent (aka neuro spicy haha).

We go down rabbit holes, research things forever, and often tend to procrastinate as soon as it's time to turn our idea into action. (let's be real the idea part of it is more fun anyway 😂)

I've been using ChatGPT and Claude since literally the minute they came out and find it insane that majority of the people still don't know or don't use AI to help them in their day to day. Just walking around being 20 IQ points lower for no absolute reason is diabolical work in my opinion.

But I hate the fact that all AI tools are linear as in they go from top to bottom. Like a book. I've always felt so constrained using them like I'm in a strait jacket.

I wanted an experience that felt more like a choose your own adventure video game. An experience where I felt free in the way I could speak to the AI to have it work with me. I could talk to it through voice or text or an image or even a video. Somewhere I could visually stitch together all my thoughts and have AI make meaning out of it.

I wanted to be able to SEE all the knowledge it had at any given point. Something that didn't hallucinate or forget my conversation every few minutes.

Another problem I had was as a content creator and a copywriter whenever I had to write something I HATED sitting there looking at an empty blinking cursor on GOOGLE DOCS or constantly switching between chrome tabs to look at ChatGPT (uninspiring linear text blob) back to Google Docs (another uninspiring linear text blob).

I wanted to be able to throw all my research together and then have the AI write for me in my own voice. What I hated about regular ChatGPT was that I couldn't do that. It would always write me something cringy in a voice that never feels like my own.

We built this because our brain thinks non-linearly. Our thoughts are a chaotic mess. We needed something to slobber our thoughts all over.

Then use AI to stitch it together and make meaning out of it.

And ultimately to produce real world published work like emails that get 100k+ opens and videos that get millions of views. Doing it in a way that saves us 100's of hours and leaves us feeling inspired for doing more work.

-Qazi

faqs.question: What is Poppy AI and what are its main features?
faqs.answer: Poppy AI is a proactive AI assistant designed to help organize your digital life by integrating various services such as email, calendar, and messaging into a single dashboard. It offers features like proactive suggestions based on your schedule and location, the ability to connect with services like Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Gmail, Outlook, iCloud Mail, Apple Health, Reminders, Contacts, iMessage, WhatsApp, Uber, and Instacart, and the capability to handle multiple content types including YouTube videos, PDFs, voice notes, and images.

faqs.question: How do I get started with Poppy AI?
faqs.answer: To get started with Poppy AI, you can sign up on their official website. Once registered, you can connect various services like your email, calendar, and messaging apps to Poppy. The platform provides a visual canvas where you can drag in content such as YouTube videos, articles, PDFs, and voice notes, organizing them into groups for the AI to process simultaneously.

faqs.question: What AI models does Poppy AI support, and how do I choose the right one?
faqs.answer: Poppy AI supports multiple AI models, each with different content limits and strengths. For instance, GPT-5 mini is suitable for quick questions, while other models may be better for analyzing extensive documents. It's important to choose the model based on your specific task to avoid exceeding token limits and encountering errors.

faqs.question: How does Poppy AI handle user data and privacy?
faqs.answer: Poppy AI encrypts user data when stored in its database and has a zero-retention policy enabled when using cloud-based large language models for its suggestions. The company aims to transition to using local, on-device AI models as technology advances to further enhance privacy.

faqs.question: What is the Power User Upgrade in Poppy AI?
faqs.answer: The Power User Upgrade is a plan designed for serious Poppy AI users, offering 16,000 total monthly credits, full API access to connect Poppy to various platforms, a chatbot feature to share knowledge without sharing your account, and white-glove setup support during the launch period.

faqs.question: How are credits used in Poppy AI?
faqs.answer: Credits in Poppy AI are consumed when you interact with the AI through chats. Each plan comes with 2,000 base credits that reset to zero on the 1st of every month at 9 AM PST. Credits are not used for uploading files or organizing boards, only for AI interactions.

faqs.question: Can I integrate Poppy AI with other applications?
faqs.answer: Yes, Poppy AI offers full API access, allowing you to integrate it with various applications. This includes building custom chatbots, connecting to automation tools like Zapier and Make.com, integrating with messaging platforms like Telegram, and embedding Poppy's intelligence into your existing software.

faqs.question: What types of content can I add to Poppy AI boards?
faqs.answer: You can add various forms of content to Poppy AI boards, including YouTube videos, PDFs, voice notes, images, and more. This allows the AI to process and analyze multiple content types simultaneously, enhancing your productivity and content creation capabilities.

faqs.question: How does Poppy AI's proactive suggestion feature work?
faqs.answer: Poppy AI's proactive suggestion feature analyzes your connected services and data, such as your calendar and location, to provide timely recommendations. For example, if it detects a 30-minute gap in your schedule near a park, it might suggest taking a walk before your next appointment.

faqs.question: Is there a community or forum for Poppy AI users to provide feedback?
faqs.answer: Yes, Poppy AI has a feedback platform where users can submit feature requests, report issues, and engage with the community. The team reviews every idea and feedback submitted to improve the product.

reviews.title: Honest Review for Poppy AI (With a Detailed Setup Video)
reviews.comment:
As a content creator juggling multiple YouTube channels and constantly looking for ways to save time, I gave Poppy AI a try after seeing it pop up with a compelling lifetime deal on AppSumo. I’ve been using it for over a month, and here’s my honest experience:

If you want a hands-on walkthrough and an honest look at real results, I highly recommend watching the Saas Guru video review:
👉 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UpsoNzJODNQ (YouTube Link)
It covers practical use cases, live demos, tips, and a direct comparison with other popular AI tools.

👍 What’s Great:

True Time Saver for Content Creation:
The workspace is incredibly intuitive—Poppy AI guides you step-by-step, whether you’re brainstorming, scripting YouTube videos, or repurposing old content into fresh blog posts. Instead of spending hours switching between notes, planners, and scripts, everything is centralized and visually organized.

Flexible & Visual Workflows:
The drag-and-drop “thought board” is a killer feature. I love mapping out video ideas, batch planning titles, and even collaborating with my small team. It feels way more organized than a Google Doc or linear AI chat.

Brand Voice Training:
I was pleasantly surprised by how well Poppy AI adapts to unique brand tones. Uploading sample content helped create scripts that actually sound like me, not just ChatGPT with generic responses.

Content Repurposing Magic:
Taking a YouTube script and spinning it into blog and social snippets is genuinely just a few clicks. The AI keeps context from the main topic, so there’s less editing after the fact. Huge productivity boost!

Support & Active Development:
The founder and team are responsive on AppSumo and in the built-in chat. Bugs and feature requests actually get noticed and worked on, which gives me confidence for the future.

👎 What Needs Work:

Learning Curve & Occasional Bugs:
At first, the visual workflow felt a little overwhelming coming from list-based AI tools. There were also minor glitches like stuck drag-and-drops and UI refreshes, but nothing that stopped my projects.

AI Credit Limitations:
Depending on your deal tier, Poppy AI works on a credit system similar to other GPT-powered tools. If you create lots of long-form content or multiple projects per week, you’ll burn through those credits faster than expected.

Occasional Output Quality Fluctuations:
While most scripts are solid, sometimes the AI outputs need a bit of rework to match my channel’s storytelling style exactly. Not a dealbreaker, but not always perfect.

Still Developing Features:
While the workspace is amazing, I’d love to see deeper integrations (like direct YouTube or WordPress publishing) and further automation for social media. I know they’re on the roadmap.

Overall:
Poppy AI really does what it promises—speeding up ideation, planning, and content creation for YouTubers and content marketers. It’s replaced three or four tools for me, and lets me focus on the creative, not tech headaches. The current lifetime deal is a no-brainer if you value time and want a genuinely visual AI workspace.

reviews.title: Useful concept, but the real cost is hidden behind expensive credits
reviews.comment:
BUB? ref: 4) You mentioned that the upselling feels too aggressive and to be completely honest with you, what happened in your account was A BUG 🐞.You called me five times 5 minutes after I registered my phone number I was forced to add in the signup!!!

Poppy has an interesting visual workflow and the ability to organise research, videos, PDFs, and content ideas on a board is useful. The core concept has potential.

However, the pricing structure seriously weakens the value of the AppSumo lifetime deal.

After purchasing, I discovered that API access is not included in the AppSumo tiers. It requires an additional Power User subscription. This matters because connecting Poppy with other AI tools, agents, and automation workflows was one of my main intended use cases.

The credit pricing is also excessive:

3,000 credits cost $150
6,000 credits cost $210
10,000 credits cost $350

These are one-time purchases, not recurring credits. Yet the upgrade page calls this an “AppSumo Lifetime Credits Deal” and refers to “lifetime credit boosts.” That wording is confusing because the credits are only added once.

The practical cost can therefore include the original lifetime deal, expensive one-time credit packages, and another recurring subscription for API access. That is very different from the value I expected from a lifetime purchase.

The upselling also feels too aggressive. I was encouraged to upgrade with messaging such as “You’re on Fire” and “Go Viral with Poppy AI” while my account still showed 0 of 1,000 credits used. That creates pressure before the product has even been properly evaluated.

Poppy may be useful for some creators, but buyers should understand the full cost structure before purchasing. For my intended workflow, the missing API access, expensive credits, unclear “lifetime” wording, and aggressive upselling make the deal poor value.

I've been using Poppy AI for a while on a lower tier from their website and upgraded to Tier 6 after seeing it land on AppSumo — and the chatbot & API feature was the deciding factor.

My use case is different from most reviewers here: I'm an (agile) consultant working with German midsize companies, not an "only one" content creator. But I'll use it for some other use cases in the feature, too.

Honesty first: on a pure ROI basis, Poppy doesn't replace my existing stack. I already run Straico (AppSumo LTD Deal :) for LLM access and n8n for automation — so the API and content generation features largely overlap with what I have. If you're already running a self-hosted automation infrastructure, be aware of this before buying.

What keeps me here — and what pushed me to Tier 6 — is two things. First, the visual board. There's something genuinely different about seeing your knowledge sources, connections, and outputs laid out spatially. It changes how I think about a project, not just how fast I execute it. That's hard to replicate in a workflow tool. It's how I can structure and see data!

Second, the chatbot & API. Giving people a dedicated AI assistant trained on the specific project knowledge base (in an easy Poppy.ai-way) I build for my online courses is a real differentiator. No Poppy account needed on their end, just a link. I'm still testing credit consumption for this use case, but the ability to choose a lighter model for Q&A helps keep usage efficient. My test (4 websites and one text field with general instructions):

13,151 -> 13,128 (Sonnet 4.6)
13,128 -> 13,099 (Sonnet 4.6)
13,099 -> 13,098 (gpt4-mini)

... looks easy 🤌​🤩​

I asked some general questions and as you can see the consumptions (in my not complex case) is nothing. It's very low level even I know, it can go up. But then simply ask the team - I think they will help to rebuild and give tips.

I also want to be transparent about why I bought at Tier 6 despite the overlap with my stack: I want to support this team. I was in an onboarding call some time ago (for my old LTD). They even send you bonus credits for just be in there. They look carefully on what you want to build and give you feedback. No selling, no pushing - this is caring! They want YOU to be successful.

They've built something genuinely good, they're bootstrapped, and they've priced this sustainably instead of racing to the bottom and then killing the LTD six months later — which I've seen happen too many times on AppSumo (looking at you, Adilo BigCommand). That kind of integrity is worth something. Don't disappoint me, please :) This is my highest invest 🫰​ I always did on AppSumo. But it feels good.

The team is responsive and honest. I asked a detailed question about credit usage for client-facing chatbots and got a straight answer — no overpromising, just clear explanation of the variables and levers to optimize. And I tested it after buying in details (see above). If I ever wanted to work again with or for a company - Poppy would be the choice ❤️

One thing I'm watching: the roadmap mention of monthly credit limits per chatbot. If that lands, this becomes a very clean B2B product, not just a creator tool. And some GDPR features like DPAs and so on. And if you bring MCP to the tiers (or some higher ones) you will made my day.

For consultants, coaches, or anyone building client-facing knowledge products: worth serious consideration. Just be honest with yourself about your existing stack first.

Downsides (hard to mention anything)
- Privacy and GDPR are the most important things here - I don't use my customer data within the app. That's something I only do on local LLMs on my own machines. But hence I does not use it with customer data directly, not an issue for me. But for all EU & German Companies there might be some open questions.
- The ChatBot needs to be CNAME covered to bring real value (for me). In my current setup it's also not much relevant.

Guys - thank you so much to be here and give us this change of being part of your fantastic product. If you need something we (at least I) can do for you, just drop a line!

Sebastian

reviews.title: The Missing Link Between Research, Learning, and AI
reviews.comment: As a lecturer, I work daily with a variety of information: academic articles, PDFs, presentations, YouTube videos, participant materials, and my own notes. At this point, Poppy AI has pleasantly surprised me. Instead of laboriously copying content back and forth between different tools, I can organize everything on a visual workspace and link it directly with the AI. The ability to utilize PDFs, videos, audio recordings, and texts simultaneously as a knowledge base is particularly helpful. This results in significantly better and more context-related outcomes than with traditional chatbots. For course preparation, I use Poppy AI to structure teaching content, create summaries, develop exercises, and generate social media posts. The visual representation aids in quickly grasping complex topics and recognizing new connections. This is especially advantageous for those who think more visually. What I particularly like is that Poppy AI not only provides answers but also supports the entire creative working process. The combination of mind mapping, knowledge management, and AI assistance makes the tool a digital thinking space. My conclusion: Those who regularly prepare knowledge and develop content as lecturers, trainers, coaches, or content creators save a tremendous amount of time with Poppy AI. For me, it has become one of the most interesting AI tools for research, knowledge organization, and content creation. People have tried for decades to organize knowledge in folders, spreadsheets, and chaotic desktop directories. Poppy AI seems to be one of the first attempts to actually solve this problem.problem.

reviews.title: The Cure for AI Chat Fatigue: Sort of a Visual Revolution
reviews.comment:
Artificial intelligence is everywhere now. It’s like we’ve all got these ghosts in the machine, and everybody is sitting around talking to screens. But those standard chat boxes? They are traps.

You try to build something big, something with a lot of moving parts, and suddenly you’re just a glorified secretary, copying and pasting and losing your mind trying to remember what the machine said five minutes ago.

You end up burning through your tokens (your digital money) just forcing the robot to remember the past. It's a waste of time and cash. But then I tested Poppy AI, and it fixed the two biggest headaches of this whole robot-talking business.

First, it gives you a visual board, which is basically a real, wide-open map. You can see every word you put in and every word it spit back out, all laid out like a big, complicated family tree.

Second, you can actually unplug things when you're done with them. You just look at a node, decide it's useless history, and disconnect it with a click. This means you stop paying the machine to remember things you've already moved past.

These visual boards change the way you work, letting you lay out these long, complicated ideas and actually see them making sense. You move faster, and you can change directions when the wind blows without losing your entire map.

Here’s a little secret from the trenches: it works remarkably well with Claude Desktop. I won't bore you with the deep nerd details today, but if you want to stretch your digital dollars, making those two talk to each other is exactly how you do it.

And Poppy isn’t just a drawing board, either. This thing can dig through the absolute noise of social media and find the actual gold, pulling up the viral posts and the ads that are actually winning. If you know what you’re looking for in your own little corner of the marketing world, those research tools are worth a whole lot of real-world cash.

I sat down for an onboarding session with Charan, and he didn't just read a corporate script to me. He showed me his own process, opened up the hood of his business, and helped me figure out how to make this tool work for my own specific situation.

The proof is in the work itself. Just this week, sitting at my desk, I've mapped out three entire, deep-dive marketing plans for niches. I built the opt-in forms, the freebies to get people in the door, the welcome emails—the whole complicated dance of getting people to listen.

Now, all I have to do is write the mix of short and long-form content that sounds like me. Except I don't. I just have to coach Poppy through some best practices to get there.

So here's the truth of it. If you've been carrying around half-cooked plans in your head for years, just letting them rattle around in the dark, you need to see them out in the light. Poppy AI gives you that light and the traction you need to finally make them real.

reviews.title: A strong tool for visual, non-linear AI workflows
reviews.comment:
I originally found Poppy months ago and had been watching it because the monthly subscription felt outside my budget. When the AppSumo deal came up, it felt like a no-brainer.

After using it and having an onboarding call with Christian Santos, I can say Poppy is not just “another AI tool” in the usual chatbot sense. Yes, it is still an AI tool, but the real value is the visual, non-linear workspace. For people who collect a lot of inspiration, work with videos, build frameworks, or think in connected layers instead of straight lines, Poppy makes a lot of sense.

My favorite use case so far is being able to add videos to a board, pull out the frameworks, keep the original videos there for later reference, and then use multiple chats on the board to mix and match context. That is much easier than trying to remember which Gemini or ChatGPT thread had “that one video” or re-uploading the same reference because I cannot remember the exact thumbnail.

The “notes for AI” feature is also a standout. I can tell Poppy exactly what part of a video I want it to mimic, extract, or use for a specific case. That makes the video more useful as directed context instead of just dumping a transcript into an AI tool and hoping it figures out what matters.

The onboarding call was excellent. Christian looked at what I was already figuring out, then expanded on it with practical tips around credit usage, focused chats, extracting frameworks, keeping assets on the board, and using context more intentionally. It did not feel canned. It felt like he actually understood how I was trying to use the software.

I also appreciate the templates, prompts, and community resources. Not because prompts are the end-all be-all, but because each AI system has its own way it wants to be spoken to. Seeing how people successfully use Poppy helps you learn the language of the tool faster.

The strongest result I have gotten so far was a set of carousels that came out beautiful and followed my design guide closely. That matters to me because I do not just want generic AI output. I need the tool to understand and preserve my creative direction.

My caveats: mobile support needs to improve, and I would love stronger TikTok/Instagram discovery by tag, niche, or adjacent content. Credit usage can also go quickly if you do not understand how context groups work, so I think Poppy would benefit from a dedicated best-practices class on token/credit usage. I would also like clearer API documentation and more education on using Poppy alongside agents or external AI tools.

Overall, I would recommend Poppy most to visual thinkers, neurodivergent or non-linear thinkers, content creators, educators, coaches, and AI power users who need a better way to organize inspiration, extract frameworks, and turn scattered context into usable outputs.

It has room to improve, but the core idea is strong. Poppy gives you a way to see and reuse your thinking instead of losing it inside endless chat threads.

reviews.title: One of the best AppSumo Offerings
reviews.comment:
Poppy AI is one of the more expensive AppSumo offerings, with an entry price of nearly $250, though members can sometimes access a discount. It is primarily aimed at content creators and allows users to gather information from multiple sources, including documents, videos, web pages, and even links to other applications. Poppy then turns that material into a knowledge base you can converse with, similar in some ways to NotebookLM or Zemith.

I originally bought Poppy AI for one reason: proposal writing. To do that well, I needed a way to organize company information, product details, prior proposals, customer requirements, and government proposal guidance in one place. When I purchased my license, AppSumo was offering a limited-time discount, and I chose to upgrade, making it a significant investment.

Before I even got started, Poppy impressed me with its support and onboarding. I was invited to a one-on-one 30-minute call, followed by a series of five live-streamed training sessions the next week. I couldn’t attend live, but I was given access to the recordings. The week after that, I received another notice about a session introducing new features. Poppy is easily one of the most engaged companies I’ve encountered.

The platform itself is straightforward: load in your sources and start asking questions. It works very well. That said, I quickly noticed that my tier two subscription was burning through credits. Part of that was because I was using a more expensive model. Another factor was the size of my knowledge base. With so many sources, Poppy had to process a lot of information every time I asked a question.

To reduce token usage, I downgraded to a smaller model and started using GPT-5.4 Mini, which still performs very well. I also asked Poppy to create a single, densely packed Markdown document containing the key information. I copied that into a Word document, saved it, disconnected the other sources, and worked from the Markdown alone. The results were still strong, but token usage dropped significantly.

I’m still a beginner with Poppy AI and only scratching the surface of what it can do. Even so, I would say it is one of the most valuable products I have purchased. The quality of the output is better than anything I’ve been able to get before.

Like any AI-based tool, Poppy.ai generates costs on the operator's side, so it runs on a credit system – and as a user, you naturally want to keep your usage efficient. OK, first off, I wasn't sure why so many people were raving about the onboarding session before raving about the product. If you've wondered the same thing, let me tell you. The onboarding call IS the product. 

I had, or so I thought, a pretty good idea about what PoppyAI did from watching various videos over the past few weeks, and having a little poke around these past 2 days, and WOWzer, so there's so much potential under the hood. Charan showed me stuff that I wouldn't have thought of doing; the eBook and lead magnet creation from your YouTube videos, for example, is a game-changer. 

We opened with tips on how not to burn through your credits and how to make your boards more efficient. 

Charan also talked 'anti-avatars' and reverse prompting, which will also save both time and credits. 

The mind mapping feature is awesome. I've been mind mapping since I was 12 years old and teaching it for the past 23 years, so to have access to something like that is right up my street and in alignment with how my brain works. 

The quality of the outputs is also superb, and I've been able to use things straight out of the gate. For example, during the onboarding, I used an 11-minute video clip from a longer 2-hour interview I watched last night, and Poppy's analysis and breakdown was spot on. 

Although I've only had PoppyAI for a couple of days, I can already see how it is like having your own researcher, assistant, copywriter, and lead magnet creator. You also get access to popular AI tools: Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, Nanobanana, all included in the price, of course within the bounds of your tier.  

If it weren't for the credits, I'd probably be on it all day!!!!  LOL. 

A few starter tips from me and notes to self, in no particular order. 

1. Disconnect items when you don't need them to be included in new chats. Why? Because if you leave everything connected, you will burn through more credits because it will run it again as a query. 
2. Add a star * the boards you use most often as your list of boards grows so that you can find them more easily. (The stars on the right-hand side of each board name).  
3. Newer AI models, all of which are included within this lifetime deal, use more credits, so check before you start which model you've selected and what you really need. 
4. Using 'Instant' creation uses more credits, so consider using medium or high if you're not on one of the top tiers. 
5. Take the time to check out the templates. Even if it's not a topic that is directly related to your industry or business, it shows the thinking and different workflows. 
6. Set up your branding. My first tests were without it, and what was produced was great, so adding your brand will next-level the information, feeling and sounding just like you. 

AppSumo, thank you for bringing us this deal. 

Team PoppyAI, well done and congratulations on a magnificent product, and wishing you every success for the future.

reviews.title: Great concept, but the credit system FOR THE SAME PDF needs urgent improvement
reviews.comment:
Great concept
Poppy AI has a lot of things I genuinely like. The visual board approach is very useful, especially when working with different sources and trying to organize research, ideas, documents, videos, and content in one place. The overall concept is excellent for content creation, research, marketing, educational material, and building workflows around source material.

One area, however, seriously weakens the experience: the way credits are consumed when working with attached documents.

When a PDF remains connected to a chat, its content is processed again with every new AI message. THIS MEANS THAT A LONG DOCUMENT CAN REPEATEDLY CONTRIBUTE TO CREDIT CONSUMPTION EVEN WHEN THE SOURCE ITSELF HAS NOT CHANGED.

For users who work with large PDFs, manuals, educational material, research papers, transcripts, or other long-form resources, this can make credits disappear surprisingly quickly. A workflow that naturally requires several follow-up questions can become much more expensive than expected simply because the same source content is being processed repeatedly.

This is not just a small pricing detail. It directly affects how freely and effectively the platform can be used for serious research and content workflows.

Poppy would be significantly stronger IF UPLOADED DOCUMENTS COULD BE INDEXED ONCE and then referenced more efficiently in subsequent questions, RATHER THAN REPEATEDLY CONSUMING CREDITS for the SAME UNCHANGED MATERIAL.

The product itself has a very strong concept and a lot of potential, and the visual workflow is one of its biggest strengths. But the current document-related credit consumption is an important weakness that should be improved, because it can make otherwise normal usage unnecessarily expensive.

. This is the ONLY but very serious reason what i give 3 stars. When you cure this please let me know and immediately I will raise my review to 5 stars.

questions.title: Chatbots consume your credits like you were chatting inside the board?
questions.comment:
I got a board and I can add the "AI Chat" box and I can chat in it privately.

Does "chatbot" mean: that same AI Chat box inside the bard can become "public" basically? Anyone with the link can chat in it, not even needing a Poppy account. Is that right? That's the only difference?

Credits 
1. Chatting on my own board in that AI chat box
2. Chatting via the public chatbot (of course connected to that same ai chat box)
Are these 2 cases EQUAL in credit consumption?

So when I sell my Chatbot to my clients, I also need to monitorate my credits in Poppy manually?
What happens if the credits run out? I guess the chatbot stops working?

children.comment:
Hey! 👋

1 - On what a chatbot actually is. You've basically got it. A chatbot is built off a Poppy board (with all its connected content) and shared with people outside Poppy 🙌

A few small differences from the regular AI chat box on the board:

- you pick the AI model the chatbot runs on instead of the user, so you can use a lighter/cheaper model for simpler Q&A
- it works on mobile (the main app is desktop-only right now) 📱
- you control exactly which board content it pulls from

2 - On credits. Yes! Whenever someone uses your chatbot it pulls from your monthly credits, same way as if you were chatting yourself. The exact burn rate per message depends on the model you picked and how much content is connected.

Heads up that we're rolling out per-chatbot credit limits soon so you'll be able to cap how much any single chatbot can use each month 🔥

Hope that helps!

Hey! Great question, this is the exact part that trips people up, so I'm glad you asked 🔥

First thing to know: a chat and a chatbot in Poppy aren't the same thing. Here's the difference 👇

A chat is the normal chat inside Poppy, where you talk with the AI directly in the app.

A chatbot is something you build from your existing chats and information in Poppy, that you can then share with clients, leads, or team members so they can ask questions and get answers too.

So having chatbot access means you can:

- share a chatbot with people who don't have a Poppy account
- embed it right on your website
- put it to work for support, sales, and your most common questions
- put it behind a paywall and sell access to your clients

Which really just means less repeating yourself, smoother support for your clients, and an easier way to help leads get what they need to say yes 🙌

---

Here are a few of my favorite ways people are actually using them 👇

🛟 Client support
A coach loaded all her program materials into Poppy and turned it into a chatbot, embedded right in her client portal.
Now her clients get answers at 11pm without waiting on her.
She answers the same five questions way less, and her people feel way more supported.
Win win.

---

💰 Sales + your DM setter
A course creator I know built a chatbot off her offer, her FAQs, and her past objections.
She dropped it right on her sales page.
Now a lead can ask "is this right for me?" and get a real answer in the moment, instead of bouncing because they weren't sure.

Then she handed that same bot to her DM setter.
He stopped pinging her every five minutes asking "what do I say to this?"
Now he just asks the bot.
Leads don't go cold waiting, and he sounds like he's been on her team for years 📲

---

🧠 Your internal team
An agency owner built a chatbot off all his SOPs, brand guidelines, and processes.
Then he shared it with his whole team.
A new hire can ask the bot how something's done instead of asking him.
He stops being the bottleneck.
It basically becomes the company's brain that everyone can tap into.

---

Hope that clears it up! Happy to go deeper on any of these 😊

children.comment: following

Yooo great question! 🔥 but It's a bit like asking how far you can drive on a tank of gas.. it totally depends on how hard you're pushing the engine! 😂

Credit use in Poppy depends on a few things:

- how much stuff you connect to the chat (this is the biggest one by far).
- the AI model you choose (some are more powerful & use more credits).
- how long your conversation history is in that conversation.
- the complexity of your prompt.

questions.title: API Question
questions.comment:
I’m recovering from surgery in the hospital rn and ran across this late, have some interest but being an avid user of openclaw unless I could integrate this with apis it doesn’t seem like this would work into my workflows but am I missing something? 

From reviews it sounds like people aren’t happy with the cost of credits for heavy users and one of the replies to the last one star review mentioned you were thinking of opening the Apis for some of the lower tiers?

children.comment:
Hey! 👋 First, hope your recovery is going smooth ❤️

You're NOT missing something, you're actually one of the people Poppy is built for. OpenClaw + Poppy is one of our favorite setups, let me break it down 🔥

1 - How OpenClaw and Poppy work together.

We have a drop-in skill called the Poppy Turbo skill. It's a single SKILL.md file that goes straight into your OpenClaw skills folder. Once it's there, OpenClaw can talk to Poppy in plain English. 

The split is:

- Poppy is the brain. Your voice, your frameworks, your past work, your sources, all loaded into a chat.
- OpenClaw is the body. It triggers, pulls live data, hands the task to Poppy, gets the answer back, and ships it.

So a real example. OpenClaw triggers on a schedule, pulls top videos and recent comments, hands all of that to your Poppy "scripts" chat as context, gets back a YouTube script written in your voice, then ships the thumbnail (nano banana) and saves the package. You don't touch it 🙌

You can also run multiple Poppy chats in one OpenClaw flow. One chat writes ad copy in your brand voice. Another chat writes the visual prompt. OpenClaw orchestrates. Three Poppy chats, one agent run, full creative package out the door.

2 - On API access. Live on Tier 5 and above.

It hits a regular POST endpoint, so anything OpenClaw can do, it can do with Poppy.

3 - On credits.

Credits only get used when the AI chat is actually generating something. They do NOT get used for importing YouTube videos, PDFs, ads, or anything else to the canvas.

How fast they burn depends on:

- the model you pick (heavier models cost more)
- how much content is connected to the chat
- how long the conversation history is

For heavy automation workflows, the big lever is which model you point each chat at + how much history you pass in. Optimizing those two stretches credits a LOT further than people expect 🙏

4 - On BYOK for heavy users.

We just pushed BYOK on Tier 4 and above 🔥

You can plug in your own OpenAI key or Anthropic key under Profile → My API Keys.
Once you turn it on, all your AI chat runs through your own account and uses ZERO Poppy credits. 

Image generation and carousel generation still use Poppy credits even with BYOK on.

If you grab Tier 6, the white-glove onboarding includes a 1:1 with me, and wiring your openclaw flows into Poppy is something we could absolutely walk through together!! 🦾🔥

questions.title: Important question
questions.comment:
Does the api support conversion threads or memory, or do i need to manage conversion history myself? 
AND ALSO, is there a way i can control how much someone consume my own credits? For example of i give access to poppy through whatsapp, can i limit his usage? And can he see how much he have left to use?, can i decide what type of ai model he will have?
I need to know how can i can control this thing so it wont get out of hand

children.comment:
Hey! 👋

1 - On the API and memory. Yes! The API supports both. You pick which one fits 🙌

Option A - No memory.
Each message you send (each API request) stands alone.
Great for automations or one-shot stuff.
If you want continuity, there are ways to stitch history into the prompt yourself.

Option B - Poppy holds the memory.
There's a way to start a thread once, save its ID, and pass that ID with every message after.
Poppy remembers everything in that thread for you.

For WhatsApp-style setups, the cleanest pattern is one conversation per user.
Each person's messages stay in their own thread and stay private to them ❤️

One more thing if you're giving multiple people access. There are two common setups:
- Use ONE trained board across all users. The bot stays personal through context you pass in (name, profile, etc.)
- Train a separate board per user. Deeper personalization, more setup on your end. Most charge a premium for this!

Both work through the API. If you grab a tier with API access (Tier 5+), we'll set up a 1:1 to figure out which one fits your setup best 🙏

2 - On limiting how many credits each person can use. A few options here:

Option A - If you're going the API route (like WhatsApp), the cleanest path right now is tracking credit usage per user in your own database.
Google Sheets, Supabase, whatever you like.
From there, there are ways to gate each message against whatever cap is set.

There's also a useful trick if you want even tighter control.
Instead of letting Poppy hold the conversation history (Option B from above), you can store the history in your own database too.
That way YOU decide how much past chat actually gets sent with each new message.
And that's the biggest factor in credits per message 🙌

Option B - If you're using our native chatbots (not the API), credits currently sit at the account level. We're rolling out per-chatbot credit limits soon so you'll be able to cap how much any single chatbot can use each month 🔥

3 - On the end user seeing how many credits they have left. They're using YOUR credits, not their own, so the balance lives on your side, not theirs.

That said, once we ship per-chatbot credit limits soon, end-user visibility on what's left in their bot is something we could add too. If that's important for your setup, feel free to drop a request on our feedback page so we can prioritize it 🙌 https://feedback.getpoppy.ai

4 - On picking the AI model for them. Yes! When you set up a chatbot you pick the model it runs on. So for simpler Q&A you can use a lighter/cheaper model to stretch credits 🙌

Hope that helps!

Hi 

- Does Poppy AI re-scan the entire canvas whenever I add something new and use tokens for it?
- Does Poppy AI have memory (remember past actions) or not?

Hey Christian!! 🙌 glad you enjoyed the video!!! thank you so much 

So here's how credits actually work: Poppy feeds the connected context to the AI with every message (that's what makes the outputs so good). So it's not a one-time "context is paid for, reuse free forever" situation, each new chat will read what's connected.

BUT here's the pro move a lot of our power users do 👉 once you've pulled the key insights out of your heavy sources (videos, docs, etc.), drop those insights into a text note and disconnect the big stuff. That way you keep the context you actually need connected without re-feeding everything and burning credits. Same quality, way lighter 🔥

Is your conversation history pretty long? that could be a reason for high credit usage as well. 

On Brands: a brand is a reusable brand voice card (not tied to one board). You build it once and can pull it into any chat on any board. So think of it as its own thing you create, not a per-board or per-workspace setup 💜

Hope that clears it up! If you want, our team can hop on and help you set up your board so it's optimized to save credits, just reach out in the support chat by clicking the purple icon on the bottom right corner of your board 👌 or email us at team@example.com  🙌
